body:
NX8's 8-bit static formats lose most on linear outputs: PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors keeps only -19.0 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) there even in its best format (fp8_e3m4). Measured on 37 models with a format search (of 666 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 21.9 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst -2.4 dB (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B). 16 of 31 models with a labelled metric lose some of it; the most: jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (agreement -1), openai/whisper-base (agreement -1) and openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo (agreement -1).

The tensors that lose most even in their best format: linear in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -19.0 dB), bmm in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -16.1 dB), bmm in openai/whisper-small (fp8_e3m4, -15.0 dB), mul in openai/whisper-small (fp8_e3m4, -15.0 dB), sin in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -14.4 dB), bmm in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -14.0 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, -13.8 dB), linear in EleutherAI/pythia-160m (fp8_e3m4, -12.1 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -12.0 dB) and bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, -10.3 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 12558 (51%), fp8_e3m4 8532 (35%), fp8_e1m6 2996 (12%), ufp8_e2m6 310 (1.26%), ufp8_e1m7 127 (0.52%), ufp8_e3m5 26 (0.11%), fp8_e4m3 1 (under 0.01%); 1.89% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where the most data carries the most error: linear in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -2.4 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, 0.9 dB) and linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, 1.6 dB).

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding and gather) needs a workaround. It affects 44 operations in 11 models: 44 calls (0.42% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in BAAI/bge-reranker-large and embedding in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions. Cost today: 0 of 44 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 44 wait for one; 150 workarounds proposed, 52 passing its check, 37 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 825 of 1883 tensors passed between kernels (44%) in 27 models: 493 for attention heads split or merged, 300 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered, 12 for dimensions merged and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 652 operations (652 calls, 6.28% of all calls; 131 G MACs, 3.69% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 198 and add → bmm (other reshapes) 80; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (199), Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (137) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (129).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 825 of 1883 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 2,370 operations in 29 models (2,370 calls, 23% of all calls), most often layernorm (661), silu (392) and softmax (371). Their quantized accuracy: worst -3.8 dB SQNR over 1,796 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 11, most 65 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 65 planned groups), over 31 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.1 powers of ten for bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (largest value 2.75e+05).

260 outputs in 12 models hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (239), select_where (18) and amin (2), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 2,370 operations limited by the LUT and up to 65 kernel launches per pass

body:
**Most costly first, the IPU architecture costs are:**

1. **Resource limits** are the most widespread cost: 2,234 operations (24% of all calls) in 27 models must go through a 256-entry LUT, costing up to -3.8 dB SQNR; kernels per pass reach 65 (stable-diffusion-v1-5).

2. **Layout conversions** affect 763 of 1,717 inter-kernel tensors (44%) in 25 models — mostly attention head splits/merges after linear — burdening 594 operations holding 127 G MACs (3.75% of all MACs).

3. **Missing instructions** block 62 operations in 14 models from running directly, dominated by run-time addressing (42 operations, mostly embeddings) and upsample (11); only cumsum has working workarounds, and none has measured cycle cost or extra kernels.

4. **NX8 format accuracy** keeps model outputs at a median 20.9 dB SQNR (worst -2.4 dB), with linear and bmm tensors in Qwen and Whisper models losing the most (down to -19.0 dB); a wider or per-row format would recover most of it.

5. **Compute efficiency** (MAC utilisation) and **IMEM use** are not yet measured, as no kernel has been built or run.
title: GLM summary

body:
**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 44 operations in 11 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 44 calls (0.42% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An upsample instruction** would put 11 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 11 calls (0.11% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**A cumsum instruction** would put 3 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 3 calls (0.03% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); recovering 0.00 dB of model output SQNR measured on 3 workarounds.

**An aten::type_as instruction** would put 3 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 3 calls (0.03% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::conv1d instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (under 0.01% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::einsum instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (under 0.01% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
